raised.claim: Any nonempty beer_ids list bypasses the whole-class scope prohibition even when the where clause contains only review_class.
raised.why_it_breaks: A proposal with scope {beer_ids:[1], where:[{col:'review_class',op:'=',value:'matcher_bug'}]} is accepted; because rowSatisfiesScope ORs the cohort and where clauses, every later matcher_bug row satisfies the scope, recreating the dumping-ground shape guard 1 is meant to reject.

raised.claim: Guard 2 is never applied to verdicts routed through new_issue_key, so a new issue can be created with rows that contradict its own scope.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a row has candidates_count=5 and its verdict references a proposed issue scoped candidates_count=0, the key check passes and the issue is created with that row attached and reviewed; only attachments to pre-existing issues call rowSatisfiesScope.

raised.claim: Model-authored issue.body can still supply an earlier triage-scope fence that silently overrides the structured scope on the next run.
raised.why_it_breaks: A body containing ```triage-scope followed by valid scope JSON is placed before the rendered block; parseScopeBlock takes the first regex match, so tomorrow's ScopedIssue uses the model-written scope rather than issue.scope, potentially accepting or rejecting rows under a scope nobody validated.

raised.claim: Saturation is checked against a fixed pre-run count and is not incremented as verdicts are grouped, allowing one batch to exceed MAX_ROWS_PER_ISSUE.
raised.why_it_breaks: An issue with postCreationRows=11 and ten accepted verdicts in this run passes the 11 >= 12 check for every verdict and receives ten more rows, ending at 21 rather than stopping after one.

raised.quote:
`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM enrich_failures
        WHERE issue_number = ? AND reviewed_at > ?`,
raised.claim: The saturation count measures only rows still present in enrich_failures, so clearing matched rows erases attachment history and reopens saturated issues.
raised.why_it_breaks: After an issue accumulates 12 post-creation rows, those beers can match and clearEnrichFailure can delete their rows; countRowsForIssue then falls below 12 and the same issue accepts another cohort, repeating indefinitely despite the historical attachment cap.

raised.claim: guardHits is not logged when the model returns a verdict for every row, even if the guards skip the entire batch.
raised.why_it_breaks: If all 50 rows receive verdicts targeting unscoped issues, covered equals orphans.length but plan.skipped is 50; the shortfall branch is skipped, so the scope_violation counters intended to expose this daily loop are never emitted.

raised.claim: The new degraded matcher_bug quiet verdicts are counted as wontfix in the persisted digest outcome.
raised.why_it_breaks: Every not_on_untappd verdict refused by guard 3 is pushed to quiet with review_class='matcher_bug'; this loop takes the else branch and increments wontfix, so a run with only unprobed absence verdicts reports them as wontfix rather than skipped/degraded matcher cases.

raised.claim: A single empty probe is treated as proof of absence even when the other probe returned hits.
raised.why_it_breaks: For a probe {brewery:'Mad Elf, MadTree', name:''}, proved is true and the terminal not_on_untappd classification survives; an empty noisy name query does not establish that the beer is absent when the brewery catalogue probe returned results, so the guard can still close a row on weak evidence.
